marks.gloss_en: תניא נמי הכי: ועוד שנה אחרת לבבל ועמד דריוש והשלימה
and there was yet another year for Babylon, and Darius arose and completed it
דכתיב: אני דניאל בינותי בספרים -- מדקאמר בינותי מכלל דטעה
Rava: Daniel too erred in this calculation
והיינו דכתיב: ... והוא פקד עלי לבנות לו בית בירושלים
לפקידה בעלמא -- [Babylon's seventy] are for mere remembrance (= p_rava_lifkida)
Rava: [the seventy 'for Babylon' are] for mere remembrance
מאי דכתיב: כה אמר ה' למשיחו לכורש
what is that which is written: 'thus says the Lord to His anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have held' (Isa 45:1)?
מכל מקום קשו קראי אהדדי: כתיב מלאות לבבל, וכתיב לחרבות ירושלים -- in any case the verses contradict each other
אמר לו רבי נחמיה: אם כן, אתה מטיל קנאה בסעודה -- unanswered in the baraita; R' Nechemya gives his own reading (אלא)
R' Yehuda: 'couches of gold and silver' (Esth 1:6) -- one fit for silver [sat on] silver, one fit for gold on gold
שונים -- משונים מיבעי ליה! the verse should say 'differing' (meshunim)
a heavenly voice: you repeat (shonim) [the use of] My vessels (= p_bat_kol_shonim)
the verse: 'and vessels differing from vessels' (Esth 1:7) -- quoted as the object of the stam's difficulty
בית הנשים מיבעי ליה! the women's feast should be in the women's house
שניהן לדבר עבירה נתכוונו (= p_shneihen_ledvar_aveira)
the verse: 'also Vashti the queen made a feast for the women in the royal house' (Esth 1:9) -- object of the stam's difficulty
one of Rav and Shmuel: 'in the court of the garden of the king's palace' (Esth 1:5) -- each guest was placed in court, garden or palace as befitted him
what is 'chur' (Esth 1:6)? Rav: [a fabric of] holes upon holes
'bahat and marble': R' Asi -- stones that vie for their owners
'dar vesocharet': Rav -- rows upon rows
'according to the law' (Esth 1:8) -- as the law of the Torah: as in the Torah's law eating exceeds drinking, so at that wicked one's feast eating exceeded drinking
'none compelled': R' Elazar -- this teaches that he gave each one wine of his own country
כתיב הכא 'יקר תפארת גדולתו' (Esth 1:4), וכתיב התם 'לכבוד ולתפארת' (Ex 28:2, of the priestly vestments) -- so Ahasuerus's glory and majesty were the priestly vestments
R' Yosei bar Chanina: 'when he showed the riches of his glorious kingdom' (Esth 1:4) teaches that he wore the priestly vestments
והיינו דכתיב: כי לא ענה מלבו (Lam 3:33)
וכי משוא פנים יש בדבר? -- is there favouritism in the matter?
הם לא עשו אלא לפנים, אף הקב"ה לא עשה עמהן אלא לפנים (= p_lo_asu_ela_lefanim)
R' Shimon ben Yochai: they acted only for appearance, so the Holy One too acted with them only for appearance
חיל פרס ומדי, וכתיב למלכי מדי ופרס -- the verses name the two nations in opposite orders
Rava: אתנויי אתנו בהדדי -- kings from one, ministers from the other (= p_rava_atnuyei)
'the army of Persia and Media, the nobles' (Esth 1:3) -- with the nobles, Persia is named first
אם כן שבשושן יהרגו, שבכל העולם כולו אל יהרגו -- if so, those in Shushan should be killed and those in all the world not; the students answer only 'you say'
the students: [that generation was liable to annihilation] because they enjoyed the feast of that wicked one
one said: he was a clever king
